messages:
mina: Opening a follow-up thread for last week's LB flare — observed rapid route-controller reconciliation that seems to trigger cross-region TLS handshake bursts and LB probe ejection. Need owners for remediation + timelines.

diego: I pulled the control-plane event stream. We saw controller reconcile loops around 2026-04-02T19:12:xx that caused ~120 rule revisions in 2m for cluster ap-south-1 -> us-east-1. Logs: ```
2026-04-02T19:12:04Z controller INFO reconcile: route mysvc changed (old=abc123, new=def456)
2026-04-02T19:12:04Z controller WARN reconcile: backpressure: queued 47 edits
2026-04-02T19:12:05Z route-sync ERROR push: apply rules failed: timeout after 5s
```

perry: That rings a bell. When route-sync hits timeouts the LB retries handshakes aggressively. We should add a short-term mitigation to debounce controller edits at the proxy level. I can own a 2-week mitigation: debounce window 10s + drop identical consecutive edits. ETA 2026-04-12.

mina: @perry assign and add metric proxy.debounce.suppressed_count. Also create an alert so oncall knows when debounce kicks in; otherwise it looks like a healthy flurry.

perry: Will do. Alert: proxy.debounce.suppressed_count > 50 for 10m -> P2. Dashboard panel: per-cluster suppressed_count heatmap.

jen: I can own LB retry policy changes. Short-term: add randomized jitter 50-250ms between TLS handshake retries and cap retries to 2 for inter-region backends. Long-term: make retry policy pluggable by cluster. ETA 2026-04-09 for rollout to canary cluster eu-central-1.

sam: Noting recurrence: found similar small bursts in 2025-08 and 2025-12. Pattern: controller churn on config updates during deploy windows. We should correlate deploys with controller churn in the postmortem doc.

mina: Can someone prototype an automated deploy-window blocker that prevents mass route flips? If not possible short-term, add CI check that avoids simultaneous route updates.

diego: I'll prototype a gate that batches route edits from the same deploy to a single commit. Prototype PR by 2026-04-07.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-2201 "Routing churn -> LB handshake ejections: debounce + jitter" https://issues.redwood/infract/INF-2201 (owners: perry, jen, diego)

mina: Summary of owners: perry -> proxy debounce + metric (due 04/12), jen -> LB retry jitter + canary (due 04/09), diego -> batching gate prototype (due 04/07), sam -> postmortem correlation + deploy window analysis (due 04/05).

perry: Deployed debounce to staging 2026-04-05T11:02Z. Quick staging smoke: suppressed_count=0 normally, simulated chatter -> suppressed_count=68 and handshake retries dropped 85%.

jen: Applied retry-jitter canary to eu-central-1 at 2026-04-06T02:30Z. Prometheus query I used for handshake rate: ```
sum(rate(lb_tls_handshake_retries_total[5m])) by (cluster)
```
Early canary numbers: cluster eu-central-1 down from 1.8% -> 0.2% retry rate over 6h.

diego: PR for batching gate: https://git.redwood/platform/pulls/534. Includes e2e test that simulates 60 route edits in 30s and asserts push latency < 10s after batching.

sam: Added deploy correlation to the postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/2026-04-lb-flare. Noted impact window: 2026-04-02T19:11:40Z - 19:35:10Z (~24m). Inter-region p95 latency spike and a small percent of client connections saw TLS handshake failures.

mina: Two open long-term items: 1) controller reconciliation root cause (race in cache invalidation), 2) modify canary playbook to include an inter-region jitter test. Volunteers?

diego: I'll dig into cache invalidation race and file a research ticket by 2026-04-20.

jen: I'll add the inter-region jitter test to canary playbook and add a checklist item for runtime-backedness. ETA 2026-04-14.

ops-bot: Weekly follow-up for INF-2201 scheduled 2026-04-08T15:00Z. Invitees: perry,jen,diego,mina,sam.

perry: Note about alerts: staging threshold should stay noisy-tolerant. Use staging alert proxy.debounce.suppressed_count > 200 for 10m. Prod: > 50 for 10m. Documented in INF-2201.

mina: Added a short reproduction guide to the incident doc for SRE/devs: use the following k8s loop to simulate flaps: ```
for i in $(seq 1 100); do kubectl apply -f route.yaml; sleep 0.2; done
```
Then run: `watch -n 2 "curl -sS https://api.redwood/healthz -w '\n%{http_code} %{time_starttransfer}\n' -o /dev/null"` to observe p95 latency changes.

sam: After staging smoke, can we schedule a 24h prod canary window in low-traffic hours before broad rollout? I recommend 03:00-07:00 UTC.

mina: Agreed. Schedule prod canary 2026-04-10T03:00Z - 2026-04-11T03:00Z in us-east-1, monitor handshake retry rate and p95 latency.

diego: Tagging @devex for CI flakiness on the batching gate tests — they were flaky on older runners.

ops-bot: Reminder: INF-2201 status check-in 2026-04-09T09:00Z.

mina: I'll close this thread once INF-2201 shows stable metrics in prod and the postmortem action items are all closed. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
